findings.issue_text: addGuests handler updates calendar using the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the organizer's, so when an attendee or team admin adds guests the organizer's calendar/video references cannot be updated and the invite stays stale; the loaded booking.user.credentials are never used
Permission check uses `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner`, so only team owners pass and admins are wrongly rejected
Any logged-in user whose email is an attendee can add unlimited guests with no cap on guests.length, creating an open email-blast vector with invite emails sent under the organizer's name
Blacklist check lowercases BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries but not the incoming guest email, so mixed-case addresses like Blocked@Example.com bypass the blacklist

Server does not dedupe guests within the request (uniqueness refine is client-side only) and the existing-attendee comparison is case-sensitive, so createMany without skipDuplicates inserts duplicate attendee rows

No check on booking status or event type: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings and to seated events without a BookingSeat row, bypassing seat limits and breaking seat accounting; the BookingListItem menu item is likewise unconditional
sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the unfiltered input instead of uniqueGuests, so guests who were already attendees receive an AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the 'guests added' notice

Attendees are committed to the DB before updateCalendarAttendees runs and that call is not wrapped in try/catch, so a calendar provider failure returns a 500 after the DB is mutated with no rollback and no emails sent

New addGuests mutation (permission logic, blacklist filtering, dedup, calendar update, email fan-out) and AddGuestsDialog/MultiEmail components have no unit or e2e tests
eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is not defined anywhere in the diff; if it does not already exist in EventManager the code will not compile
Booking query includes user.credentials (loading every credential row including keys) for the organizer but never uses them
catch block logs 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' without the error object, making email failures undiagnosable

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests handler updates calendar using the caller's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the organizer's, so when an attendee or team admin adds guests the organizer's calendar/video references cannot be updated and the invite stays stale; the loaded booking.user.credentials are never used

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched including `user.credentials` (`include: { user: { include: { ... credentials: true }}}`), but those credentials are never used. Instead, the code calls `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and constructs `EventManager` with `...user` where `user` is the *caller* (`ctx.user`). Since the handler explicitly allows non-organizers (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner) to add guests, this means calendar updates (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`) will run with the caller’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, which can prevent updating the organizer’s connected calendar event and leave invites stale when the caller isn’t the organizer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission check uses `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner`, so only team owners pass and admins are wrongly rejected
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify that the permission logic incorrectly uses `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner`, requiring both roles instead of allowing either; this wrongly rejects admins and should be `||`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Any logged-in user whose email is an attendee can add unlimited guests with no cap on guests.length, creating an open email-blast vector with invite emails sent under the organizer's name

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation allows any authenticated user to add guests if they are an attendee on the booking (`isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((a) => a.email === user.email)`, and the permission gate allows `isAttendee`). The input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only enforces `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no maximum length, and the handler does not impose any cap or throttling before creating attendees (`createMany`) and sending emails (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`). This makes it feasible for an attendee to submit a very large `guests` array and trigger a large volume of outbound emails associated with the organizer/event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check on booking status or event type: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings and to seated events without a BookingSeat row, bypassing seat limits and breaking seat accounting; the BookingListItem menu item is likewise unconditional

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation/handler updates `booking.attendees` unconditionally for any bookingId the user can access. In `addGuests.handler.ts` there is no check of booking lifecycle state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) nor any time-based check (past bookings). It also doesn’t enforce or update seat accounting: it always `createMany` attendees and never creates/updates any seat-related rows, despite the code explicitly carrying `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` from `booking.eventType` into the CalendarEvent. On the UI side, the new BookingListItem menu option `add_members` is added to `bookingOptions` without any condition on booking status/type, so users can attempt this action in all cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the unfiltered input instead of uniqueGuests, so guests who were already attendees receive an AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the 'guests added' notice

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts, the server filters the requested emails into `uniqueGuests` (excluding already-existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only creates attendees for `uniqueGuests`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the original unfiltered `guests` input. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` checks `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Passing unfiltered input means an already-existing attendee whose email was included in the request will match `includes(...)` and incorrectly receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the “guests added” notice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendees are committed to the DB before updateCalendarAttendees runs and that call is not wrapped in try/catch, so a calendar provider failure returns a 500 after the DB is mutated with no rollback and no emails sent

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no `try/catch` and no DB transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., calendar provider/API failure), the TRPC mutation will reject and the client will see an error while the database has already been mutated (no rollback). Because `sendAddGuestsEmails` happens after that call, it will also not run in this failure path (the email `try/catch` does not cover the calendar update).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Read-then-write without a transaction or unique constraint allows two concurrent requests adding the same guest to both pass the already-attendee filter and both insert

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code first reads the booking and its current attendees, then computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering only against the *currently loaded* `booking.attendees`. It then performs a separate `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. There is no transaction around the read+write and no server-side de-duplication of `guests` (the input schema is only `z.array(z.string().email())`, unlike the client-side refine), nor is `createMany({ skipDuplicates: true })` used. As a result, two concurrent requests can both pass the `!booking.attendees.some(...)` check before either write happens and then both attempt to insert the same attendee rows (leading to duplicates if no DB uniqueness, or a unique-constraint error if there is one). This matches the finding’s core issue: a non-atomic check-then-insert.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New addGuests mutation (permission logic, blacklist filtering, dedup, calendar update, email fan-out) and AddGuestsDialog/MultiEmail components have no unit or e2e tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new UI, TRPC mutation, and email templates, and it does not include any new test files or modifications to an existing test suite. However, the proposed finding claims there are “no unit or e2e tests,” which is not strictly verifiable from this diff alone (tests could already exist elsewhere or be added in a separate commit), and in any case a lack of tests is a quality/process concern rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the shown code changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is not defined anywhere in the diff; if it does not already exist in EventManager the code will not compile

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a call to `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` in `addGuests.handler.ts`, but the `EventManager` class implementation is not part of this diff (it is imported from `@calcom/core/EventManager`). The fact that the method is not defined *in the diff* does not mean it does not already exist in the codebase. Therefore, the finding relies on speculation about code خارج the shown changes and is not a verifiable defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking query includes user.credentials (loading every credential row including keys) for the organizer but never uses them

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the prisma.booking.findFirst() call includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }`. Later code uses `booking.user?.destinationCalendar` when building `evt.destinationCalendar`, but it never reads `booking.user.credentials`. Credentials are instead fetched via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. So the query is indeed loading organizer credential rows unnecessarily (including sensitive fields) without using them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: catch block logs 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' without the error object, making email failures undiagnosable

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` catch block discards the caught `err` and logs only a static string. This makes email-sending failures difficult to diagnose because no error details/stack are recorded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow with `booking.userId || 0` turns a booking without a user into an unhandled Prisma throw (500) instead of a proper TRPCError

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is loaded via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. The `|| 0` indicates `booking.userId` may be falsy/nullable; if it is `null/undefined`, the query becomes `id: 0`, which will not exist and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma error. That throw is not converted to a `TRPCError` (unlike the explicit `if (!booking) throw new TRPCError(...)` earlier), so it would surface as an unhandled/internal error (500) instead of a controlled TRPC error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: email-manager.ts references calendarEvent.team?.members but the handler never populates team on evt, so team hosts never receive the notification for team bookings
organizer-add-guests-email subject uses this.calEvent.attendees[0].name, but newly added guests have empty names, so the subject can render as 'with  at ...'

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the subject uses `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. In the added guests flow (`addGuests.handler.ts`), newly created attendees are inserted with `name: ""` (see `guestsFullDetails`). The `CalendarEvent` passed to email uses `attendees: attendeesList` derived from DB attendees, which now include these blank names, and there is no guarantee the first attendee has a non-empty name (Prisma include order is not specified). Therefore the subject can legitimately render with an empty name (e.g., "... with  at ...").

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog error message is always a non-empty string (e.g. 'undefined: ...'), making the t('unable_to_add_guests') fallback dead code and exposing 'undefined:' prefixes to users

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, the onError handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;`. Because this is a template literal, `message` will always be a non-empty string (e.g., if `err.data?.code` is undefined it becomes `'undefined: ...'`, and even if `t(err.message)` returns an empty string it still yields at least `'undefined: '`). Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the fallback translation, and users may see an `undefined:` prefix when `err.data?.code` is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog never resets isInvalidEmail on successful submit or when dismissed via overlay/escape (onOpenChange), so the error banner persists on reopen; the email list is likewise not reset on overlay dismissal

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation in `handleAdd`, but it is never set back to `false` on a successful mutation (`onSuccess` only closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`). Also, the `Dialog` uses `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, so dismissing via overlay click/escape only toggles `isOpenDialog` and does not reset either `isInvalidEmail` or `multiEmailValue`. Therefore, after an invalid submission (or any stateful input), closing via overlay/escape and reopening will show the error banner and/or previous emails, matching the finding.
